posts.topic: Choose the one renewal question you want answered first
posts.text:
If your renewal is on your mind, what is the one question you would like to ask first?

It might be, ‘Which part of this renewal should I look at first?’ Or, ‘What would you need from me to talk through this?’ You do not have to turn that first question into a polished explanation. Write it in your own words on a note you keep for yourself.

When you contact Morrison Insurance, begin with the general topic and ask what information would be useful next. Keep policy numbers and document photos out of public comments. A first message is a starting point, not a request to post your paperwork.

Our Start Here page helps you choose a starting route for your question: https://morrison-ins.net/start-here

No need to share your renewal details here. Keep your question handy for a direct conversation.

posts.topic: Find the coverages, limits and deductibles before asking a comparison question
posts.text:
If you are looking at an auto renewal, where do you find the details you want explained?

The Texas Department of Insurance says the declarations page summarizes your coverages, dollar limits and deductibles. That gives you a place to look for the wording behind your question, without trying to work through every page at once.

Keep that page for your own reference. Pick one heading you would like explained and write down a question such as, ‘Can you help me understand this deductible?’ If you are comparing another quote, ask which details should be lined up before you compare the price.

Our existing auto quote checklist is here: https://morrison-ins.net/resources/car-insurance-quote-checklist-center-tx

Please do not post your declarations page or policy details. Ask the team how to share any needed information directly. A general explanation is not a decision about your particular coverage.

posts.topic: What happens inside the shed? Describe use rather than rely on a building label.
posts.text:
What happens inside the shed?

A building name is only the beginning. A detached space might hold garden tools, be a place for a personal hobby, or have a different use than it did last year. You do not have to decide what insurance category fits before asking a question.

For a first conversation, make a short private list: the building, what happens there now, and what has changed. Leave out serial numbers, addresses, values, and photos of your belongings when commenting online.

TDI notes that home coverages vary by company. Your own policy and a conversation with your agent matter.

Our home and rural-property guide is a general starting point, not an answer about your particular shed. Bring one use question, not your whole filing cabinet.

posts.topic: When is the change happening? Separate a repair, a planned change and a new use.
posts.text:
Planning a repair or changing how a room is used? Start with the timeline, not a stack of paperwork.

On a private note, separate three things: what is planned, what is underway, and what is already finished. Then add whether the space will be used differently afterward. A roof repair and turning a room into a workspace are different questions to describe, not conclusions to make online.

Ask your agent: “What would you need to understand this change, and when should we talk?” Confirm the next step during that conversation rather than assuming a deadline or an answer.

Our preparation page offers general prompts you can use without entering personal information. Keep project addresses, contractor documents, and financial details out of comments.

Start here: https://morrison-ins.net/prepare-for-a-conversation

posts.topic: Who will use the space? Describe guests, stays and payment without labeling the answer.
posts.text:
“Someone will stay here” can mean several different things.

If you are thinking about a guest room, a separate space, or letting someone stay for a while, describe the plan in plain language. Is it an occasional visit or an ongoing arrangement? Is any payment involved? Has the plan started, or are you still considering it?

Those are questions to bring privately to your agent, not a way to decide coverage from a social post. You do not need to share a guest's name, travel dates, address, or payment details here.

For an opening message, try: “I have a question about a planned change in who uses part of my property.” Then ask what information to bring and confirm next-step timing.

Our what-to-expect page explains the conversation handoff: https://morrison-ins.net/what-to-expect

posts.topic: What is the land actually used for? Start with routines, not an acreage label.
posts.text:
A rural address is not the whole description of a property.

For a useful first conversation, think about what happens on the land now. Is it mainly a place to live? Do you keep animals, grow something for your household, store equipment, or have an activity that involves sales? You can describe more than one use without trying to decide which insurance label belongs on it.

Make a private list of the routines, any recent changes, and one thing you want to understand. Acreage by itself is not the question we are asking you to answer here, and this post cannot determine a policy fit.

Our start-here page offers a home and rural-property route for that first question. Keep exact locations, animal counts, equipment details, and documents off social media.

If someone has asked for insurance paperwork, try: “I have a request to discuss. What information do you need, how should I share it, and when should I follow up?” You can explain the general purpose first without posting a contract or identifying a customer.
